claims.text: Applying a high-alumina Al2O3 refractory ceramic coating to hot-dip aluminum plating components will significantly reduce erosion during long-term exposure to high-temperature liquid aluminum.
The initial components are uncoated metal sinking rollers, pulling rollers, or guide plates.
A high-Al2O3 refractory ceramic coating is deposited on the components before molten-aluminum exposure.
The coating forms a dense ceramic layer.
The ceramic layer acts as an inert barrier to liquid aluminum.
The ceramic barrier impedes chemical attack by liquid aluminum.
The ceramic barrier impedes physical erosion by liquid aluminum.
Al2O3 ceramic coatings resist chemical reactivity with molten aluminum.
Al2O3 ceramic coatings resist high-temperature corrosion.
The coating protects the underlying metal substrate from erosion by molten aluminum.
Coated components will exhibit less surface erosion than uncoated metal components under molten-aluminum exposure.
Coated components will have a longer service life than uncoated metal components under molten-aluminum exposure.
Uncoated metal components undergo rapid corrosion and erosion during routine hot-dip aluminum plating.
Repeated thermal cycling may limit coating effectiveness by affecting coating adherence or durability.
Mechanical stresses may limit coating effectiveness by affecting coating adherence or durability.
Direct evidence is insufficient regarding long-term industrial performance, optimal coating thickness, and durability of high-Al2O3 refractory coatings in hot-dip aluminum plating.
